user.description: How would you like to set up your inverter?

manual.title: Inverter connection
manual.description: Enter the inverter's IP address, Modbus TCP port (default 502) and Modbus unit ID (default 1).

scan.title: Scan network for inverters
scan.description: Scans the chosen subnet for hosts that have Modbus TCP port 502 open. Hosts whose MAC address belongs to a known SunSpec inverter manufacturer are listed first. The scan only does a TCP connect probe, it never sends any Modbus bytes, so it will not interfere with other Modbus devices on the network. The default subnet is detected from the Home Assistant host's network configuration.

scan_results.title: Pick your inverter
scan_results.description: These hosts answered on Modbus TCP port 502. Hosts marked 'SunSpec vendor' have a MAC address from a known inverter manufacturer and are most likely your device.

serial.title: Modbus RTU connection
serial.description: Configure a serial-line (RS-485) connection to a SunSpec-capable inverter. Typical setup is a USB-to-RS-485 adapter on /dev/ttyUSB0 (Linux) or COM3 (Windows). Baud rate is usually 9600 or 19200 - check your inverter's manual.

wilan.title: FoxESS Smart WiLAN datalogger
wilan.description: Configure a connection to a FoxESS Smart WiLAN (or WLan-WW) WiFi datalogger. The datalogger does not serve Modbus TCP; it relays Modbus frames over its HTTP interface instead. Enter the datalogger's IP address and the Modbus unit ID of the inverter behind it (1 on most devices). Reads only at the moment: register writes are not yet available over this connection.

data.unit_id: Modbus unit ID of the device behind the datalogger

settings.title: Inverter settings
settings.description: Pick which SunSpec models to expose as sensors and optionally set the inverter's peak AC power for plausibility filtering.

data.max_ac_power_kw: Peak AC power of the inverter (kW, optional)

data_description.max_ac_power_kw: Readings above this are discarded as implausible. Pre-filled from the inverter's own nameplate with 20% headroom, because inverters overshoot their continuous rating and DC power always reads above AC output. Do not lower it to the bare nameplate: the DC power and apparent power sensors would then read "unknown" for most of a sunny day. Clear the field to switch the filter off.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure inverter connection
reconfigure.description: Update the host, port or unit ID of an existing SunSpec inverter without losing its history. The new connection is probed and the entry is only updated if the inverter still reports the same serial number.

error.connection: Cannot reach the inverter. Check the host, port and unit ID, then try again.
error.timeout: Timed out reaching the inverter. The device may be offline or another Modbus client may be holding the connection.
error.device_error: The inverter responded with a Modbus error. Check that the device firmware is up to date.
error.invalid_subnet: The subnet is not valid CIDR notation, or it is too large to scan (use a /22 or smaller).
error.no_candidates: No hosts with Modbus TCP port 502 open were found in this subnet.
error.no_models_selected: Select at least one SunSpec model. Saving an empty selection would stop the integration from polling the inverter and all sensors would disappear.
error.unique_id_mismatch: The inverter at this address reports a different serial number than the one you originally configured. Refusing to swap your sensor history onto a different device.
error.sma_unit_id: The inverter answers SunSpec on unit ID 126, not on the one entered. SMA puts SunSpec at its own Modbus unit ID plus 123. The field has been set to 126; submit again.

host_options.title: Connection settings
host_options.description: Edit the inverter's host, port and unit ID. The next step lets you change which SunSpec models are exposed as sensors and the peak AC power for plausibility filtering.

model_options.title: Device options
model_options.description: Select which SunSpec models (data registers) you want sensors for. The peak AC power is optional and used to discard unrealistic values that some inverters report at dawn or dusk (e.g. spikes in the MW or TWh range). Leave it empty to disable filtering.

data.scan_delay: Pause between models while scanning the SunSpec model tree (seconds). The tree is only scanned when the integration has to build a new connection and no stored layout still matches the device, never on a normal poll, so this pacing costs nothing in normal operation. Raise it if scans fail on slow hardware, lower it only if the rescan itself is disruptive.
data.capture_raw_registers: Capture raw modbus bytes for diagnostics
data.max_ac_power_kw: Peak AC power of the inverter (kW, optional)
data.write_beta_enabled: Enable experimental export controls (BETA: export limit, power factor and grid connection from models 123 / 704, and the set_export_limit action). Off by default. Read the docs before enabling; writing to the wrong Modbus register can lock you out until a physical reset. The battery controls of model 124 do not need this.
data.release_slot: Release the Modbus connection between polls
data.standby_when_idle: Inverter powers down when idle (no repair notification while it is unreachable)
data.rearm_on_change: Re-apply the export limit and power factor by switching them off and on when their value changes (Fronius)
data.fronius_web_password: Web interface password (Fronius, the local "customer" login)
data.fronius_web_forget: Forget the stored web interface login

data_description.fronius_web_password: Unlocks what a GEN24 tells its own web page and not Modbus: temperatures, the battery's identity and cell temperature, where the smart meter sits, the grid charging flags, whether Modbus control is allowed, and a Modbus reset. The password is not stored; a hash of it that logs in to this inverter and nothing else is. Leave the field empty to keep the stored login.
data_description.rearm_on_change: A Fronius GEN24 takes a new export limit or power factor only when its enable switch goes from off to on. With this on, changing a value while its switch is on writes the switch off, the new value, and the switch on again, one second apart, so for that second the inverter runs without the limit. Off: the value is written on its own and the inverter keeps the old one until the switch is turned off and on, by you or by an automation.
data_description.release_slot: Off is recommended. The integration keeps one Modbus session open, which is what Modbus TCP is designed for and what inverters handle best. Turn this on only if another program outside Home Assistant has to read the same inverter and cannot go through a Modbus proxy. Taking turns on a single connection is unreliable, and many inverters refuse new connections when asked for one every few seconds.
data_description.max_ac_power_kw: Readings above this are discarded as implausible. Pre-filled from the inverter's own nameplate with 20% headroom, because inverters overshoot their continuous rating and DC power always reads above AC output. Do not lower it to the bare nameplate: the DC power and apparent power sensors would then read "unknown" for most of a sunny day. Clear the field to switch the filter off.
data_description.standby_when_idle: Leave this off unless you need it. The integration already detects an inverter that reports OFF, SLEEPING, SHUTTING_DOWN or STANDBY before the connection drops, and stays quiet about that on its own. Turn this on for a device that goes off the network without warning, or that does not publish an operating state at all. While it is on, the "Cannot reach SunSpec inverter" repair is never raised. Sensors still go unavailable when the inverter has been away for a few minutes, and a device that answers with a Modbus error still reports it.
data_description.usage_stats: On by default. Once a day the integration tells the author's server that an installation is active. It sends a random install ID, the version of the integration and of Home Assistant, the vendor profile and the number of entries. It sends no host, serial number, model, location or readings. Turn it off to send nothing.

error.no_models_selected: Select at least one SunSpec model. Saving an empty selection would stop the integration from polling the inverter and all sensors would disappear.
error.connection: Cannot reach the inverter right now. Wait a moment and try again, or check the device is online.
error.web_auth_failed: The inverter rejected that web interface password. It is the local "customer" login of the inverter's own web page, not the Solar.web account.
error.web_unreachable: The inverter's web interface did not answer on port 80.

transport_error.message: Cannot reach the SunSpec inverter at {host}:{port}: {error}

protocol_error.message: Device at {host}:{port} does not speak SunSpec: {error}

device_error.message: SunSpec inverter at {host}:{port} returned a Modbus exception: {error}

transport_error.title: Cannot reach SunSpec inverter
transport_error.description:
The integration cannot connect to the SunSpec inverter at {host}:{port} (unit ID {unit_id}). Three consecutive update cycles have failed.

Last error: {error}

Things to check:
- The inverter is powered on
- The inverter is reachable on the network (try ping {host})
- No firewall is blocking TCP port {port}
- No other Modbus client is hogging the inverter's single TCP slot

protocol_error.title: Device does not speak SunSpec
protocol_error.description:
The integration reached the device at {host}:{port} (unit ID {unit_id}) but it does not respond as a SunSpec device.

Last error: {error}

Things to check:
- The device actually supports SunSpec (some Modbus devices use a vendor-specific register map)
- The unit ID is correct (some inverters use unit ID 1, others use 0 or 247)
- The device firmware is up to date - older firmware sometimes has broken SunSpec implementations

device_error.title: Inverter reports a Modbus exception
device_error.description:
The SunSpec inverter at {host}:{port} (unit ID {unit_id}) responded with a Modbus exception. Three consecutive update cycles have failed.

Last error: {error}

Things to check:
- The inverter is in a normal operating state (not in fault mode)
- The selected enabled models match what the inverter actually supports
- Download diagnostics from this integration and attach them to a bug report

cjne_conflict.title: cjne/ha-sunspec is still active
cjne_conflict.description:
SunSpec 2 cannot start up for the inverter at {host}:{port} (unit ID {unit_id}) because the cjne/ha-sunspec integration is still actively running for the same device.

KACO Powador and most other SunSpec inverters only allow ONE Modbus TCP connection at a time. cjne is currently holding that connection, so SunSpec 2 cannot poll the device. Running both integrations against the same inverter would also produce duplicate sensors and unstable values.

To migrate from cjne to SunSpec 2:

1. Open HACS and uninstall the cjne/ha-sunspec integration
2. Restart Home Assistant
3. SunSpec 2 will retry automatically and pick up the existing entities

Your entity IDs and Recorder history will be preserved by the SunSpec 2 migration helper.

stale_model.title: SunSpec model {model_id} has gone missing
stale_model.description:
The inverter at {host}:{port} (unit ID {unit_id}) was previously exposing SunSpec model {model_id}, but it has now been missing from every scan for {missing_minutes} minutes.

This usually means the inverter dropped the model permanently (firmware update, vendor reconfiguration, or the underlying hardware module was disconnected). The associated sensors are still in your entity registry but will stay on their last good value.

If you no longer need them, open the device-info page for the affected device and use the trash-can icon to remove the device. The matching entities will be cleaned up automatically.

If the model comes back on its own, this Repairs issue will clear automatically on the next successful read.

set_battery_plan.name: Set battery plan
set_battery_plan.description: Update plan settings together. Changes apply on the next successful poll; disabling stops the plan immediately.
